definitions.explanation: Body coloring that lets an animal blend into its surroundings so that predators or prey cannot easily see it. A biology term, also used figuratively for anything that helps someone go unnoticed.

examples.japanese: カメレオンは{保護色|ほごしょく}を{持|も}つ。
この{虫|むし}は{葉|は}っぱと{同|おな}じ{保護色|ほごしょく}をしている。
examples.english: This insect has protective coloration the same as the leaves.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}の{中|なか}では{白|しろ}い{毛|け}が{保護色|ほごしょく}になり、{敵|てき}から{身|み}を{守|まも}る。
examples.english: In the snow, white fur becomes protective coloration and protects them from enemies.

notes:
A biology term for coloring that camouflages an animal against its background. Contrast with {警告色|けいこくしょく} (warning coloration), which makes an animal conspicuous.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {保護色|ほごしょく}をしている: to have protective coloration
- {保護色|ほごしょく}になる: to serve as camouflage
- {周|まわ}りの{保護色|ほごしょく}: camouflage matching the surroundings

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {迷彩|めいさい}: camouflage pattern — man-made, as on military uniforms and vehicles
- {擬態|ぎたい}: mimicry — imitating another object or creature in shape as well as color
